stem.text: A type of firework is made by connecting two rockets, facing in opposite directions, to a rod, as shown.
The rod is attached to a frictionless pivot so that the firework can rotate in a vertical plane.
The firework has weight $W$. The pivot exerts a force $R$ on the rod that is equal and opposite to $W$.

stem.alt: Diagram of a rod with a pivot, with a rocket at each end; forces R and W act at the pivot, and force F and distance d are marked for each rocket.

stem.text: Each rocket exerts a force of magnitude $F$ on the rod at a perpendicular distance $d$ from the pivot. The forces exerted by the rockets are always in opposite directions.

A.text: The firework is in equilibrium because the resultant force acting on it is zero.

B.text: The firework is in equilibrium because the resultant torque acting on it is zero.

C.text: The firework is not in equilibrium because the resultant force acting on it is not zero.

D.text: The firework is not in equilibrium because the resultant torque acting on it is not zero.
